uncertain.explanation: The PR moves got from ^15.1.0 to ^16.1.0, a major version change, but leaves the HTTP/2 options in readStatus untouched: `http2: true`, `request: http2wrapper.auto`, and `agent: {http2: relayAgent}` (an http2-wrapper Agent). This hints that got 16 may have changed or removed its http2-wrapper-based HTTP/2 path. If so, `http2`, `agent.http2` or the custom `request` function could be rejected, ignored, or behave differently. Possible outcomes: health polls fail option validation, or they fall back to HTTP/1.1 and the shared relayAgent (maxSessions: 4) stops being used, so closeClient no longer controls the connections. I couldn't read got 16's release notes or docs, so this is an inference from the lockfile only. Before merging, check got 16's breaking changes for `http2`, `agent.http2` and `request`, and add a test that calls readStatus against an HTTP/2 endpoint.

reported.title: `agent: {http2: false}` turns off HTTP/2 session reuse; the old code reused one pooled session
reported.explanation:
Before this PR, the code passed `new http2wrapper.Agent({maxSessions: 1})`. That kept one pooled HTTP/2 session and reused it across calls to readSnapshot. The got v16.0.0 release notes say `agent.http2` "is only an opt-out flag now: pass `false` to skip session pooling" (source: release notes). Setting it to `false` therefore turns pooling off. It does not translate the old agent into the new API.

What I infer from the code (not tested): every readSnapshot call, and every retry, would open a new TLS and HTTP/2 session instead of multiplexing over one shared session. That adds a handshake to each request, which counts against the 2.5 s `timeout.request` limit, and it opens more connections to the snapshot server.

To get the closest match to the old behavior, delete the `agent` option so got uses its built-in pooled session cache. Then `http2: true` is all that's needed. I can't confirm from the docs whether got 16 can cap the pool at exactly one session.

reported.title: Commander 15 no longer defaults `color` to true when both --no-color and --color are defined, so colors are off by default
reported.explanation:
Documented fact: the commander 15.0.0 changelog lists a breaking fix (#2405): "only lone `--no-*` option sets default option value to `true`, default not implicitly set when define both positive and negative option in either order".

Code evidence: src/cli.ts defines both `.option('--no-color', ...)` and `.option('--color', ...)`. It then calls `success(text, Boolean(options.color))`. Under commander 14, defining `--no-color` first made `options.color` default to true. Under ^15.0.0, when neither flag is passed, `options.color` is undefined, so `Boolean(undefined)` is false. `success` in src/format.ts then returns the label without ANSI color.

This contradicts README.md line 4: "Colors are on by default". Fix: set the default explicitly, e.g. `.option('--color', 'Enable colors', true)`, or use `options.color !== false`.
